Key Characteristics & Etiology: Birth weight <2500g regardless of gestational age; Preterm <37 completed weeks
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Immaturity of organ systems surfactant deficiency impaired thermoregulation and renal function
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Hypothermia hypoglycemia respiratory distress feeding intolerance; Red Flags: Apnea necrotizing enterocolitis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Gestational age scoring (Ballard) blood glucose SpO2 monitoring; Thermal care + KMC + parenteral/enteral feeding

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Perinatal asphyxia or birth depression requiring immediate resuscitation within 60 seconds
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Interruption of placental gas exchange leading to hypoxia hypercapnia and secondary apnea
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Apnea gasping or cyanosis HR <100 bpm limp muscle tone; Red Flags: HR <60 bpm despite effective PPV
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: APGAR scoring continuous heart rate monitoring; Provide warmth + PPV with room air (21%) + 3:1 chest compressions

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Unconjugated or conjugated hyperbilirubinemia; Pathological if onset <24 hours of life
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Immaturity of hepatic UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) enzyme or ABO/Rh isoimmunization
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Jaundice progressing cephalocaudally lethargy poor feeding; Red Flags: Opisthotonos high-pitched cry (Kernicterus)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Serum total and direct bilirubin blood group/Coombs test; Intensive Phototherapy (460-490 nm) + DVET

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Onset <72 hours of life from vertical intrapartum transmission (GBS E. coli Listeria)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Invasive bacterial bloodstream infection triggering SIRS and pulmonary alveolar flooding
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Temperature instability (hypothermia/fever) lethargy grunting tachypnea (RR >60) poor suction
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Blood culture FBC (I:T ratio >0.2) serial CRP CXR; Empirical IV Ampicillin + Gentamicin

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Perinatal asphyxia resulting in systemic hypoxemia and reduced cerebral blood flow
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Primary energy failure followed by secondary reperfusion injury neuronal apoptosis and cerebral edema
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Stage I (Hyperalert) Stage II (Lethargy seizures hypotonia) Stage III (Stupor coma flaccid)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: aEEG / EEG cranial ultrasound MRI brain; Therapeutic Hypothermia (33.5C for 72h initiated within 6h)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Significant delay (>2 SD below mean) in 2 or more developmental domains in children <5 years
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Genetic chromosomal environmental or structural brain insult impairing neurodevelopment
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Failure to achieve age-appropriate gross/fine motor speech or social milestones; Red Flag: Hand preference <12 months
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Developmental screening tools (Denver II / ASQ) chromosomal microarray MRI brain; Multidisciplinary intervention

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Trisomy 21 (meiotic nondisjunction in 95% of cases) associated with maternal age
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Gene dosage effect from extra chromosome 21 material disrupting organogenesis and neurodevelopment
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Up-slanting palpebral fissures epicanthic folds flat nasal bridge single palmar crease sandal gap hypotonia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Karyotype / Chromosomal microarray Echocardiogram (40% AVSD); Early intervention + cardiac surveillance
